issues.description: Basic-usage example fetches node via next() over a generator instead of by name or index, teaching value/identity confusion.
issues.detail: All three reviewers flagged `next(n for n in pipeline.nodes)` to grab 'the training node'. It ignores the node's name, returns whatever iterates first, and models the wrong identity as the pipeline grows. Use `pipeline.node("train_model_node")` or at minimum `pipeline.nodes[0]`. This is the first example readers copy.

issues.description: ImagePreview example has unreachable code after the first return with no warning to the reader.
issues.detail: The `preview_correlation_matrix` function returns the URL form, then presents a commented data-URI alternative as 'Or' below the return. Readers skim and see two options when only one is reachable. Split into two clearly named functions or restructure as if/else so each example is self-contained and runnable as written.

issues.description: Framework behavior of `node.preview()` (return type, None case, exception policy) is never stated.
issues.detail: Examples call `training_node.preview()` and `preview.to_dict()` as documented API but never specify what happens when `preview_fn` is unset or raises. The 'wrap in try-except if needed' best practice pushes failure semantics onto every author instead of stating the framework's one policy. State once what `node.preview()` returns on missing/failing preview_fn.

issues.description: Data-context guidance complects preview view, node compute, and dataset I/O without stating the closure invariant.
issues.detail: The section admits previews have no input access, then suggests closures or 'access datasets within the preview function'. The closure example captures `sample_data` by reference with no statement on snapshot-vs-live aliasing, and the dataset-access suggestion quietly permits I/O inside preview_fn. Either pass values explicitly, copy at construction (`list(data_sample)`), or document aliasing.

issues.description: `meta` field conflates general metadata with renderer configuration in one bag.
issues.detail: Docs describe `meta` as both run facts (timestamps, versions) and rendering instructions (Mermaid layout, syntax highlighting language). Different consumers, different lifetimes, place-oriented thinking. A separate `render_config` field would decomplect; one bag invites confusion about which keys are facts vs renderer directives.

issues.description: Experimental warning and content schemas (Plotly/Custom/renderer_key) are under-specified.
issues.detail: The experimental warning does not enumerate which surface (`preview_fn` kwarg, `preview_contract` module, `node.preview()`) is unstable. Plotly/CustomPreview content shapes use literal ellipses, and `renderer_key` describes a backend/frontend coupling with no namespace or fallback contract. Either link to `preview_contract` or provide minimal concrete values and one sentence on registration.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a competent docs-only PR for an experimental `preview_fn` feature, but the example code teaches bad habits that users will copy. Consensus P1 issues: the basic-usage snippet retrieves nodes by generator instead of by name, the ImagePreview example has unreachable code after a return, the framework's behavior for `node.preview()` on missing or failing preview_fn is never stated, and the data-context guidance complects preview/compute/IO without stating closure invariants. P2 concerns center on the `meta` field carrying two unrelated concerns and under-specified content schemas plus the experimental surface area. Fix the example code, state one failure policy, and tighten the contracts.
